cases.reason: The reference line every binding must reproduce byte for byte. A binding that emits members in another order, or inserts whitespace, fails here first.
Every optional member present at once. Pins the full member order, which a case using only the required four cannot.
Field keys are emitted in code-point order, not the caller's insertion order. A binding that passes the map through unsorted produces a different line for the same event.
1.0 and 1 are the same JSON value. JavaScript cannot tell them apart and Python can; the rule is integral VALUE, so both accept and both emit 1.
Non-ASCII is emitted literally. Python's json.dumps escapes by default, so a binding that omits ensure_ascii=False fails this and nothing else.
A string field value is refused — the structural redaction guarantee. If this passes, the envelope has somewhere to put a secret.
A non-integral number is refused. 1.5 is expressible in both languages, unlike 1.0 which is not distinguishable in JavaScript.
JSON has no NaN literal; a value overflowing to Infinity is the expressible form. A binding checking only 'is a number' admits it.
2^53+1 is the first integer a double cannot represent exactly. Paired with the 2^53-1 case this pins the safe-integer bound, which Python — whose ints are unbounded — has no native reason to enforce.

Naive Python emits -0.0 where JavaScript emits 0. The integral-value narrowing already fixes this, so this is a regression pin on that narrowing — a binding that skips it passes every other numeric case and fails here.
The largest integer a double represents exactly is accepted — the upper edge of the safe range.
Negative integers are in range; the bound is symmetric.
Zero is a value, not an absence. A binding using falsiness to test presence drops this field.
Booleans are one of the two admitted value types.
An empty fields map is present-but-empty, and is emitted rather than dropped. A binding treating it as absent produces a shorter line.
null is neither a boolean nor an integer. A binding checking only 'not a string' admits it.
Nesting would reopen the envelope: an arbitrary object has unlimited places to put a secret.
An array is an object in JSON terms and must be refused for the same reason as a nested object.
fields itself must be a map. The reason is invalid-fields, not invalid-field-value: there is no member to attribute it to.
Field keys are lowercase. A binding matching case-insensitively accepts this.
Underscore is not in the field-key alphabet, which is narrower than the event-name alphabet.
Sixteen fields is the limit and is accepted — the boundary is inclusive.
Seventeen exceeds the limit. Paired with the sixteen case, this pins the boundary as inclusive rather than exclusive.
ts is required. A binding defaulting it to the current clock would make the encoder impure and pass this silently.
Python's datetime.isoformat() default. The single most likely wrong timestamp a Python binding emits.
timespec='milliseconds' is the obvious fix for the microsecond case and is also wrong: +00:00 is not Z.
Valid RFC 3339, refused here: lowercase breaks the plain string sort the canonical form exists to guarantee.
The fraction is fixed-width, not optional. Omitting it breaks fixed-width string comparison.
Arabic-Indic digits. A binding whose regex engine makes \d Unicode-aware — Python's and Rust's do — accepts this and passes every other timestamp case.
debug is a published level.
info is a published level.
warn is a published level.
error is a published level.
The level set is closed. trace is a plausible fifth level and is not one.
Levels are lowercase; a binding upper-casing for display must not accept the upper-cased form back.
The empty string is refused.
Emptiness, not blankness: no trimming is defined, so no two languages' disagreement about trim can reach this contract. A binding reaching for trim() fails here.
Event names are lowercase dotted segments.
Underscore is not a segment separator; the dot is.
Hyphen is not a segment separator either.
A doubled dot makes an empty segment. A binding splitting on '.' and checking each part must reject the empty one.
Every segment starts with a letter.
audit is the second published kind, and is what the audit-logger migration targets.
The kind set is closed, like the level set.
correlationId is optional and its absence emits no member — the line has no null placeholder.
Explicit null is not absence. Python's dict.get() collapses the two, so a binding using it accepts this.
64 characters is the limit and is accepted — the boundary is inclusive.
65 exceeds the limit. Paired with the 64 case this pins the boundary as inclusive.
The alphabet is URL-safe. An address-shaped id is the leak this bound exists to slow down.
An error carries a code and nothing else by default.
code is the one required member of error.
A free-form message is exactly what the envelope refuses to carry — it is where an exception string, and the row data inside it, would land.
A stack trace carries file paths and, in some runtimes, argument values.

An unknown member is refused, where negotiation/cases/hello-unknown-member.json requires the opposite. That inversion is the redaction guarantee: the hello frame is open for forward compatibility, the envelope is closed because an open envelope has unlimited places to put a secret.
null is not an event. The path is empty because no member is at fault.
An array is not an event either — typeof [] is 'object' in JavaScript, so a binding testing only typeof accepts it.
Two faults at once. §5's order makes unknown-member reachable first; a binding validating ts before scanning members passes every single-fault case and fails only here.
The decode direction round-trips: the parsed event omits `nimbus`, which is what makes encode(parse(line)) reproduce the line.
A line that is not JSON is refused before any member is inspected, and is distinguishable from a well-formed line carrying a bad member.
A hello frame on the diagnostic stream is refused by discriminator, not by member validation. Pins that the two message families cannot be confused.
An absent discriminator is wrong-message, not not-object: the line parsed fine, it is simply not a diagnostic.
Closedness applies on the way in as well as out. A gateway that validates only on encode would accept a leaking line off the wire.
A level above the threshold passes the filter.
'At or above' includes equality. A binding using a strict > drops every event at exactly the configured level.
A level below the threshold is filtered out.
